findings.issue_text: Migration inserts old embeddable_hosts setting values verbatim via raw SQL, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization, so values like 'http://discourse.org' never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host's URI host comparison and sites silently lose embedding after upgrade

Migration's execute(...)[0]['id'] for the embed_category lookup assumes a row exists; when embed_category is unset or doesn't match a category name, the empty result raises NoMethodError and aborts the migration mid-run
EmbeddableHost before_validation calls self.host.sub!(...) which raises NoMethodError on nil host instead of failing validation, causing a 500 on create requests with missing/blank host

Migration interpolates the site-setting host value directly into INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}') with no quoting, breaking on single quotes and creating a SQL injection vector; should use quote(h) or a parameterized insert

EmbeddableHost.record_for_host uses where("lower(host) = ?", host) without downcasing the bound value, so mixed-case referers like 'http://EvilTrout.com' never match and legitimate embeds are rejected

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embedding_controller#update performs no mutation and just re-serializes the fetched @embedding, making the client's saveChanges a silent no-op that falsely reports success

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, but it only `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and does not read params or persist anything. On the client, `admin-embedding` controller defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, issuing a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` (via the new `admin/adapters/embedding` pathFor). Since the server-side update action performs no mutation, that PUT cannot save any changes and will always just re-serialize the same `@embedding`, making `saveChanges` effectively a no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In store.js.es6 plural hydration branch, `delete obj[k]` runs unconditionally (unlike the singular branch), so a missing sideloaded collection yields an array of undefined and destroys the original *_ids, leaving the record with no usable data

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `store.js.es6` the new plural branch (`/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]`) always does `obj[k].map(...)`, assigns the result to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`, and then **unconditionally** `delete obj[k]`. Unlike the singular branch (which only deletes when hydration succeeds), this will remove the original `*_ids` even if `_lookupSubType` can’t find any sideloaded records in `root` (producing an array of `undefined` values). That’s a real correctness regression: the record can lose the only reliable identifiers when sideloading is missing/incomplete, and the code doesn’t guard against `obj[k]` not being an array either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In store.js.es6, `hydrated || []` is dead code because map always returns an array

adjudication.rationale: In the new `_hydrateEmbedded` plural-ID branch, `hydrated` is assigned from `obj[k].map(...)`. If that line executes successfully, `Array#map` always returns an Array object (truthy), so `hydrated || []` will always evaluate to `hydrated`, making the `|| []` fallback unreachable/redundant. This is a minor redundancy (style/nit), not a functional bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6 hydration calls obj[k].map(...) assuming the *_ids value is an array; a null or scalar value throws a TypeError and breaks the entire find/findAll

adjudication.rationale: In store.js.es6, the new plural-handling branch for keys matching /(.+)\_id(s?)$/ does `obj[k].map(...)` when `m[2]` is truthy (i.e., for `*_ids`). This assumes `obj[k]` is always an Array. If the payload provides `*_ids: null`, `*_ids` omitted but present as `null`, or any non-array scalar, `.map` will throw a TypeError and can break hydration for the whole record load. The diff adds this behavior without any guard like `Array.isArray(obj[k])` or defaulting to `[]` before mapping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation or DB index on host, so duplicate rows are accepted and record_for_host's non-deterministic .first makes the embedded topic's category arbitrary

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` records as the source of truth for allowed embed hosts and per-host category selection (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import` does `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` then uses `category: eh.try(:category_id)`). However, `EmbeddableHost` has only a format validation and the migration `create_table :embeddable_hosts` adds no UNIQUE index/constraint on `host`. The admin controller `save_host` also doesn’t check for existing records before saving. `record_for_host` queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` with no ordering, so if duplicates exist, which row is returned (and thus which category is chosen) is not guaranteed. This makes the category assignment potentially arbitrary when duplicates are present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_spec.rb 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test no longer exercises anything meaningful (has_topic_embed? unstubbed, embed_truncate unset) since the condition was removed from expandable_first_post?; should be deleted or rewritten

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Topic#expandable_first_post?` to remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check, so *if* there is still a spec asserting behavior based on “embeddable_host(s) blank”, that spec would indeed be obsolete. However, in the provided diff hunk for `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the `expandable_first_post?` tests are not shown (the diff is truncated right as that section begins), and no test named/worded like “is false if embeddable_host is blank” is visible. Without the actual test present in the diff, the finding cannot be verified as a real problem introduced/left by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb only asserts class inheritance, with no coverage of create/update/destroy, the uncategorized-category fallback, or rejection of non-staff users

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb, and it contains only one example: `it "is a subclass of AdminController"` asserting `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`. The controller itself implements `create`, `update`, and `destroy`, includes `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff`, and `save_host` contains an uncategorized fallback (`host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?`). None of these behaviors (CRUD actions, fallback, or authorization restrictions for non-staff) are exercised by the added spec, so the finding is directly verifiable in the diff as a test coverage gap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingSerializer's has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids emits embeddable_host_ids without sideloading the host objects (needs include: true), so the client's plural hydration resolves ids to nothing and the admin table renders empty rows
rest.js.es6 uses type.replace('_', '-') which replaces only the first underscore, so multi-underscore admin model names won't match their ADMIN_MODELS entry; should use replace(/_/g, '-')

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the only relevant admin models are 'site-customization' (type likely 'site_customization') and the newly added 'embeddable-host' (type likely 'embeddable_host'). Both contain only a single underscore, so `type.replace('_', '-')` is sufficient to match the corresponding `ADMIN_MODELS` entries. The proposed issue would only manifest for a type with multiple underscores and a matching multi-dash `ADMIN_MODELS` entry, which is not present in this diff, so the finding is speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb declares `resources :embeddable_hosts`, generating index/show/new/edit routes the controller doesn't implement, raising AbstractController::ActionNotFound; should restrict with only: [:create, :update, :destroy]

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the line `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` generates the full RESTful set of routes (index/show/new/edit/create/update/destroy). But `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` in the diff only defines `create`, `update`, and `destroy`—no `index/show/new/edit`. Hitting the generated GET routes (e.g. GET /admin/embeddable_hosts) would route to missing actions and raise `AbstractController::ActionNotFound` (typically surfaced as a 404/exception depending on environment). Restricting the routes with `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]` (or implementing the missing actions) would avoid that mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable-host.js.es6 destroyRecord().then(...) lacks a .catch(popupAjaxError), so a failed delete leaves the row in place with no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); });` but provides no `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (unlike `save()`, which does). If the delete request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and no user-facing error is shown; also `deleteHost` is not sent, so the row remains, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration uses create_table ... force: true, silently dropping any existing embeddable_hosts table, and its DELETE FROM site_settings inside a `change` migration is irreversible, so rollback destroys the original configuration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration defines `change` but performs non-reversible data operations via `execute`, including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Rails cannot auto-reverse arbitrary SQL in a `change` migration, so rolling back will raise an `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` and the deleted configuration cannot be restored automatically. Additionally, `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will drop an existing `embeddable_hosts` table if present, which is a destructive operation.
